symptom: Two official CI verify runs failed one new synthetic test because it expected strict SDK verifyJsonReadback to accept a pathname with a substituted symlink ancestor. Raw pathname reads followed the symlink to valid decoy JSON, but the existing strict SDK reader correctly rejected the ancestor. The test expectation was corrected and a later official CI passed; no Linux publication or production failure was demonstrated.
lesson: A raw filesystem read that follows an ancestor symlink is not equivalent to the existing strict SDK verifyJsonReadback contract. That SDK checks real directory ancestors with lstat before opening a single-link regular file; the test falsely expected it to accept valid decoy JSON through a substituted ancestor. Distinguish object-relative FD readback, raw pathname reads, and strict SDK pathname admission in both fixtures and reports.
guardrail: Before writing a new readback race assertion, inspect the actual SDK readback implementation and freeze separate expected outcomes for raw path traversal, strict ancestor-symlink rejection and pinned-FD object reads. Do not weaken assertRealDirectoryAncestors to satisfy a fixture, infer canonical-path reachability from FD identity, retry the unchanged incorrect assertion, or claim production/BUY authority from synthetic Linux tests. Keep full CI payload, process exit, workflow, post-job and runner evidence separate.
